query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance and microscopic deformation of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate during sliding in the high-temperature operating regime are governed by the coating's grain boundary structure and its evolution under thermal and mechanical stresses.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating with a specific grain size and grain boundary structure
generation.intervention: Controlled change in grain boundary structure through varying annealing temperatures and times
generation.conditions: High-temperature operating regime (above 500°C) with sliding contact
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary structure and its evolution
generation.mechanism: Thermally activated grain boundary diffusion and sliding-induced grain boundary migration
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance and reduced microscopic deformation with optimized grain boundary structure
generation.baseline: As-deposited coating with a random grain boundary structure
generation.boundary: Grain boundary structure evolution as a function of annealing temperature and time
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative relationship between grain boundary structure and wear resistance/deformation

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled annealing experiments with varying temperatures and times, followed by sliding wear tests at high temperatures
measurements: Grain boundary structure characterization using electron microscopy and diffraction
Wear rate and microscopic deformation measurements using profilometry and scanning electron microscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant correlation is found between grain boundary structure and wear resistance/deformation, the hypothesis is falsified

limitation.phenomenon: governing mechanisms of wear resistance and deformation

prior_attempts: investigations into wear resistance and deformation
